summary: Project Potatospace123 is an analytical framework and visualization tool designed to identify and characterize new terrestrial analog sites on Earth for permanent lunar bases and Martian exploration. Addressing the challenge, we cross-reference open space data from NASA Earthdata, Moon Trek, and Mars Trek to match extreme Earth environments—such as arid deserts, volcanic fields, and subterranean lava tubes—with the geological, thermal, and topographical conditions of planetary landing sites. This project is crucial because finding accurate, accessible Earth analogs allows space agencies and engineers to safely stress-test rovers, equipment, and habitat technologies before committing to costly space missions. By bridging planetary science with clear digital visualization, Project Potatospace123 streamlines site selection for future human exploration.
details:
Identifies and characterizes new terrestrial analog sites on Earth, such as extreme arid deserts, volcanic fields, and subterranean lava tubes, that share environmental and geological characteristics with permanent lunar base locations and Mars. The project cross-references open space data to match Earth terrain features (like slope gradients, thermal fluctuations, and soil composition) with planetary mission requirements.

By locating and documenting these terrestrial analogs, our project gives mission planners, engineers, and researchers accessible testing grounds on Earth to safely stress-test rovers, equipment, and habitat designs before space deployment.

We utilized Canva for mapping visualizations and presentation design, alongside open datasets and tools including NASA Earthdata, Moon Trek, and Mars Trek.

We focused on discovering high-value, overlooked terrain types (such as volcanic caves offering natural radiation shielding) while maintaining strict scientific honesty by factoring in the differences between Earth's gravity and Martian/lunar environments.
